title: Italian Business-to-Business Invoicing Data: A Network Analysis
abstract: We present a comprehensive description of the network of Italian Business-to-Business commercial relationships, based on the universe of electronic invoices collected by the Italian Tax Office. The firm-to-firm detail of the data is exploited to describe the distribution of the numbers of buyers (customers) and sellers (suppliers) per firm, the centrality of each firm in the production network, and the average distance between firms. We characterize for the first time the firm-to-firm network describing the Italian production system, and present its geographic and sectoral breakdown. The analysis reveals heavy tailed distributions for the numbers of buyers and sellers per firm, implying a scale-free structure of the network. The distributions of centrality values display heavy tails as well, indicating a strong concentration of importance in a relatively small number of firms. We estimate the tail exponents for all these distributions, finding in all cases lower exponents for downstream (buyer-side) distributions than for the upstream (seller-side) ones.
summary: This paper analyzes the structure of the Italian B2B commercial network using electronic invoicing data. By applying network science, it finds the network is scale-free, meaning a few highly connected firms dominate the economy. The study provides detailed insights into the concentration of economic importance across sectors and regions.
main_problem: The paper characterizes the structure of the Italian production network by analyzing the B2B commercial relationships derived from electronic invoices.
main_result: The network exhibits a scale-free structure, indicated by heavy-tailed distributions for buyer/seller counts and centrality, with distinct differences observed between upstream and downstream connections.
method: Network analysis techniques are employed, including calculating network metrics (density, mean degree), analyzing degree distributions via power-law fitting, and computing various global centrality measures (e.g., PageRank).
model_or_system: The system is the directed, weighted network of Italian Business-to-Business (B2B) commercial relationships, where firms are nodes and invoices represent weighted, directed links.
key_observables: Distribution of buyers/sellers per firm, network centrality measures, tail exponents of degree distributions, network density, and mean degree.
important_parameters: The analysis is sensitive to the transaction threshold (invoice amount), which dictates the connectivity of the network.
main_assumptions: The analysis is based on the assumption that the B2B invoicing data provides a comprehensive view of the production system, though the structure is noted to be vulnerable to targeted shocks.
figures_summary: Figures summarize global centrality measures (by province/sector), the variation of network metrics with transaction thresholds, and the fitting of degree distributions to power laws.
paper_structure: The paper moves from establishing the data source and general network properties (density, mean degree) to detailed analyses of centrality measures, sector-by-sector and province-by-province breakdowns, and finally, structural analysis based on transaction thresholds.
why_interesting: While the subject is economics, the methodology relies heavily on complex network theory, power-law scaling, and structural analysis of connectivity, which shares mathematical parallels with critical phenomena and complex systems studied in statistical mechanics.
